$comment: Editorial operating data: clusters, cadence, guide registry and nav labels. The generator reads this to build the front page, cluster pages, sitemap and feed, so the nav labels the brief asked to settle live here rather than in scattered templates.

nav.note: Brief asked for reader-facing navigation plus every dashboard surface reachable from the footer inside one nav group; the reader bar stays at four links and the workroom collapses into one group.

cadence.rule: One guide each Tuesday 07:00 CET; the desk note on the first Tuesday of the month.
cadence.queue_policy: Upcoming topics are an unranked list. The next topic is chosen from the first block of Search Console queries that matches a cluster, not from preference.
cadence.added_to_findability: Every accepted guide is appended to sitemap.xml and feed.xml by the generator; publishing a guide and updating findability are the same commit.

season.editorial_note: Counter-space and oven-style questions rise when the oven is already busy; capacity questions rise before hosting. Treat as timing for publishing, not as a claim about search volume.

clusters.name: Capacity
clusters.question: How much of the basket is actually usable?
clusters.why: The single most common regret, and the one a headline number obscures.

clusters.name: Cleanup
clusters.question: What has to be washed, and how often?
clusters.why: Decides whether the appliance is used weekly or monthly.

clusters.name: Counter space
clusters.question: Where does it live between uses?
clusters.why: Footprint plus clearance is a real constraint that no review score captures.

clusters.name: Multi-function
clusters.question: Does the extra mode replace a device or duplicate one?
clusters.why: Where marketing value and household value most often disagree.

clusters.name: Power & noise
clusters.question: What does the label say about draw, and what is it like at 19:00?
clusters.why: Two things a buyer discovers after purchase rather than before.

clusters.name: Reading a listing
clusters.question: Which fields on a product page are verifiable, and which are decoration?
clusters.why: It is the skill our own verification process is built on, so we publish it.

guides.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
guides.dek: Two shapes, two failure modes. The trade-offs that decide it are on the listing if you know which fields to read.
